items.title: New literary prize Prix Pascal launches in France for manuscripts written with AI
items.excerpt: A new French literary prize will recognise a manuscript written with artificial intelligence, requiring entrants to disclose the tools and methods used to produce their work.

items.title: Tomato Novels Announces Full Shutdown of All AI-Related Services
items.excerpt: ByteDance-backed web-fiction platform Tomato Novel is shutting down its AI writing services and switching new low-level authors to full-work-completion signing after a flood of AI-generated serials; authors pushed back and some open-sourced their AI workflows.

items.title: "검색창서 책 펼친다"…밀리의서재, AI로 독서 진입 간소화
items.excerpt: KT 밀리의서재가 검색 결과에서 도서 핵심을 요약해 보여주고 바로 독서·추천으로 이어지는 'AI 브리핑' 기능을 도입했다.

items.title: Meta tries to scapegoat staff who downloaded torrents to spare execs
items.excerpt: In the authors' book-piracy suit, Meta was ordered to name the executives who approved torrenting books for AI training; Meta argues nobody 'decided' to pirate books.

items.title: “저작권 신탁기구 추진…AI의 ‘책 도둑질’ 막아야”
items.excerpt: 앤트로픽의 국내 도서 대량 매입·해적판 다운로드 논란 속에 한국출판인회의가 AI 학습 이용을 관리할 저작권 신탁기구 설립을 추진한다고 밝혔다.

items.title: "내 책 썼는지조차 몰라"…AI 학습 우려에 경고음 커지는 출판계
items.excerpt: 국내외에서 AI 학습용으로 의심되는 도서 대량 구매가 잇따라 포착되면서, 자기 책이 학습에 쓰였는지조차 알 수 없는 작가·출판계의 우려가 커지고 있다.

items.title: From Content to Trusted Knowledge: Reflections on Frankfurt Book Fair 2026
items.excerpt: Reflections from Frankfurt 2026 on how publishers can turn trusted content into useful knowledge in an AI-mediated landscape, and help people act on it.

items.title: [Korean Startup Interview] Sodalive: Turning Finished Webtoon Characters into AI Creators
items.excerpt: Sodalive is pivoting from its voice platform VoiceOn to turn official webtoon and web-novel characters into AI creators that keep producing content after a series ends.

items.title: Iceland Considers AI for New Teaching Materials
items.excerpt: Iceland's education minister says AI could play a role in producing new school teaching materials, though options and funding remain undecided.

items.title: Why Are Publishers Suing Big Tech With One Hand and Embracing AI With the Other?
items.excerpt: An essay from an Authors Guild panel on authorship and AI, asking why publishers litigate against AI firms while quietly adopting AI in their own workflows.

items.title: Is It or Isn’t It? How Generative AI is Poisoning the Literary Well For Everyone
items.excerpt: After Vauhini Vara's Atlantic piece suggesting a prize-winning story was probably AI-written, Lit Hub examines how AI-detection suspicion is corroding trust in literary work.

items.title: Thélyson Orélien denies using AI to write novel but admits to plagiarism in earlier work
items.excerpt: Canadian author Thélyson Orélien has denied using AI to write his prize-winning novel C’était ça ou mourir, but admitted to 'unacceptable' plagiarism in earlier work.
